appraisal_events.evidence: « Il est immonde »... « je ne me sens pas en sûreté avec ça chez moi »... « il est dans les griffes de ce Jupien... un ancien forçat »... « Il mourra assassiné un jour ou l'autre »
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme Verdurin savagely maligns Charlus to Brichot as part of her scheme to separate him from Morel; the narrator notes she has 'un certain don d'improvisation quand la malveillance l'inspirait,' framing the specific slanders as her own inventions even as the plotting itself is real.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Elle a engagé Morel chez elle où on redonnera le même programme, et je pense même à demander une invitation pour M. Verdurin. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus singles out M. Verdurin alone for a future invitation at Mme de Duras's, a distinct personal favor pointedly withheld from his wife.

appraisal_events.evidence: « Les duchesses... se rattrapaient, faute de mieux, en étouffant des fous rires devant les tableaux d'Elstir »
appraisal_events.explanation: Bored aristocratic guests, disappointed the salon was not stranger, mock Elstir's paintings; the narrator's framing presents this as revealing the guests' philistinism rather than endorsing any real critique of the painter.

status_effects.explanation: A scheme is set in motion behind his back to sever his hold on Morel, with his hostess denouncing him in severe terms, though the narrator undercuts the reliability of the specific accusations.
He alone among the Verdurins receives Charlus's favor of a future invitation, a small personal inclusion independent of his wife's public exclusion.
His paintings become an object of stifled mockery for uncomprehending guests, though the narrator's irony toward the duchesses weakens the force of the judgment against Elstir himself.
